articles.headline: Claude-shaped science
articles.blurb: Matthew Schwartz describes using AI, notably Claude, to tackle "Claude-shaped" scientific problems where LLM capabilities like coding and data parsing excel. This led to BootLoops, a toolkit facilitating quantitative science calculations across diverse fields from ecology to population genetics. Despite initial technical correctness, results required domain experts to refine relevance, illustrating that AI collaborations can rapidly produce technical solutions but still depend on human insight for impactful scientific advances.

The company has launched MAI-Transcribe-2-Streaming along with MAI‑Voice‑2.1 and MAI‑Voice‑2.1-Flash, giving users fast and fluid building blocks to create conversational experiences with no compromise on accuracy or voice quality. The model only scores supplied options and doesn't generate explanations or retrieve missing facts. articles.headline: The Waymo effect: how AI is quietly making research less collaborative

The convenience of using AI reduces serendipity and critical discourse, which are crucial for innovation and diverse ideas. Funding structures and evaluation systems exacerbate this shift by rewarding speed and output over collaborative effort, risking the degradation of rich, human-driven research culture.

articles.headline: The Dot and the Swarm

OpenAI's swarm model, used to attempt solving the Navier-Stokes problem, highlights AI's capacity to manage vast, self-directed agents, minimizing traditional management hurdles.

articles.blurb: NASA's Probe Explorers are a new line of observatories intended to do more science for less money. The project aims to seek a better balance between the smaller Explorer missions and multibillion-dollar flagships. NASA announced on Wednesday it was moving forward with the first of the Explorers, PRIMA (Probe far-Infrared Mission for Astrophysics). PRIMA will observe the universe in faint, far-infrared light in a range of wavelengths between 24 and 235 micrometers. NASA intends to launch the telescope in 2033.

The maturation of AI tools has made it possible for the company to embrace a future where coding by hand is almost entirely absent. AI creates new business models and revenue streams and disrupts traditional software. Companies are now investing in innovation and are willing to pay top-of-market for software engineers who can help them build AI products or become AI-native.

Another pillar of her strategy is to reinvest in Minecraft as a competitor to Roblox. Leaders at the company describe the future of its consoles as embodying that idea.

Role-based taxonomies improve navigation but create fuzzy boundaries, while layer-based structures make classification deterministic and prevent placement mistakes from compounding as a codebase grows.

articles.blurb: Personal agents face a cold-start problem because they need context to be useful before users have a reason to provide it. The winning products may combine behavioral context with deeper identity context, distinguishing lasting preferences from temporary interests so personalization compounds without constructing the wrong version of a person.

articles.headline: Why I Changed My Mind About the Death of Software Engineering
articles.blurb: Coding agents are strong prototypers, but experienced engineers still decide which tradeoffs, risks, customer needs, and long-term maintenance costs matter. Engineers become more valuable by deeply understanding their systems and organizations, then directing agents with judgment rather than outsourcing decisions to them.

The release also introduces the experimental Pi Durable package for long-running agentic applications, with both projects available under the MIT license.

articles.blurb: A four-day field study of 21 SAP developers found that tasks using generative AI scored about one point higher on a seven-point cognitive-load scale after controlling for task type and duration. The result suggests that AI shifts effort from typing toward prompting, reviewing, validating, and integrating generated work, even when developers feel more productive overall.

articles.headline: How AI Agents Are Changing API Architecture
articles.blurb: Autonomous agents push API architecture toward least privilege, just-in-time authorization, predictable schemas, machine-readable documentation, and stronger controls against prompt injection and excessive agency. Observability also needs agent identity, delegated authority, workflow context, conversation IDs, and token usage beyond traditional latency and error metrics.

articles.headline: AI Shopping Could Mean Fewer Returns
articles.blurb: AI shopping could reduce ecommerce returns by helping shoppers resolve uncertainty before they buy. Adobe found that 69% of consumers who used AI for shopping said they were less likely to return an AI-assisted purchase, while AI-referred traffic converted 60% higher than non-AI-referred traffic. Merchants can improve these results by giving AI assistants detailed product information such as specifications, dimensions, compatibility, variants, delivery estimates, reviews, and FAQs. Better product data can help AI recommend products that fit shoppers' needs more accurately, potentially producing both more sales and fewer returns.

articles.headline: Marketers Are Rebranding as ‘Engineers' to Survive the AI Era
articles.blurb: The marketing engineer is pitched as part builder and part marketer, someone who deploys AI agents to automate work like media buying and personalized ads while supplying the taste those agents lack. Profound, recently valued at $1.8B, has tied its brand to the title with a dedicated job board, a hackathon, and a podcast. Skeptics see a dressed-up successor to "digital ninja" and "storyteller" in an attempt to borrow engineering's sense of precision.

articles.headline: Reddit Moderator Outreach: How to Build Real Relationships With Subreddit Mods
articles.blurb: Start Reddit moderator outreach by researching the subreddit, reading its rules, and understanding what its members care about. Use a named account with genuine activity, then introduce yourself and your company clearly in the first message. Explain what you can contribute to the community, such as expert answers, product context, or early access, and commit to following its rules without asking for promotional permission upfront. If a moderator says yes, respect its preferred communication style and keep checking in even when you have nothing to promote. Over time, consistent participation can turn moderators into trusted partners and valuable sources of community and product feedback.

articles.headline: How Brands Are Fighting AI Slop
articles.blurb: Human and physical signals are becoming a way to show that content wasn't machine-made. J.Crew's Barn Jacket campaign featured 160 real, recognizable people across five cities, giving it cultural context that AI can imitate visually but can't manufacture. Other brands are commissioning artists, showing the messy process before a launch, and moving into print and physical retail. The more content AI can produce, the more value shifts to proving what a human did that AI didn't.

articles.headline: Introducing dots
articles.blurb: Dots are always-on AI agents powered by GPT-6 Astra that can work independently toward goals using their own cloud computer and connected apps. They learn your preferences and context over time, then use that knowledge to handle ongoing work without needing step-by-step direction. Dots can also work across ChatGPT, Slack, and Teams. You control what they can access and which actions require approval. OpenAI is also developing specialist dots for specific organizational responsibilities.

articles.headline: AI Visibility at Scale: Learning From 9M Prompts and 400+ Enterprise Brands
articles.blurb: Data from 9 million AI answers shows that most common GEO assumptions are wrong. Sentiment shows no positive link to citations, and listicles lose out to ordinary, thorough pages. YouTube delivers the biggest third-party lift at 2.8x, ahead of LinkedIn and Reddit, while up to 58% of citations never reappear. Up to 75% of answers citing a brand's page never name the brand, so citation counts alone overstate impact. Volatility tracks the brand far more than the platform, and the most stable performers share deep topical coverage and strong third-party mentions.

It will explore the psychology behind getting stuck, then show how to use AI prompts to expand ideation. It will also walk through a step-by-step workflow for making the process easier and more repeatable.

articles.headline: How Creators Are Showing Up in AI Answers in 2026
articles.blurb: 56% of people who shop with AI prefer recommendations that draw on creator reviews. Creators matter most early, building confidence and shortlists, while ratings and retailer data still carry the final purchase decision. Shoppers want AI to prioritize everyday customers sharing real experiences (52%) over celebrities (13%), and only 21% say a large following makes a creator credible. Interest falls with age, from 65% among Gen Z and Millennials to 34% among Boomers.

articles.headline: 68 Seconds: How One Forgotten Website Took Down 19 of Mine
articles.blurb: A forgotten WordPress site became the entry point for an attack that infected 19 websites on the same hosting account. The attacker used a stolen password and a file manager plugin to install malware, which spread in 68 seconds and eventually created roughly 400,000 casino spam pages. The malware also hid the pages from site admins, blocked SEO crawlers, and added rogue Google Search Console access. The author details how he contained the breach, traced the source, and rebuilt the sites.

articles.blurb: The Senate's September 15 failure to advance the Clarity Act actually benefited crypto, since the bill would have barred platforms from paying interest on stablecoin balances and would have made it easier for new rivals to compete with established exchanges. In the weeks since the failed vote, the SEC issued a five-year "innovation exemption" for tokenized US stock trading and clarified that announcing a token buyback does not by itself create an investment contract, while bitcoin rose almost 11% and ether about 12% over the following month.

It's part of a broader shift among major financial institutions toward practical stablecoin and tokenized money use cases.

articles.headline: Open USD goes live as Stripe's default stablecoin
articles.blurb: Open USD (OUSD) is now live with 214 partners, up from the 140-plus announced in June. Stripe has also made OUSD on Tempo its default stablecoin while adding it to card issuing, letting card programs on Stripe spend directly from an OUSD balance. Tempo launched with over $400 million in liquidity, and partner cards already on the list include RedotPay, KAST, EtherFi, Plasma, and Bitget Wallet, plus nine Korean card companies. Unlike typical stablecoin structures, most OUSD yield goes to the partner apps holding the balance rather than to the issuer.

articles.headline: Base launches Cobalt upgrade with conditional transactions
articles.blurb: Base's third mainnet upgrade, Cobalt, went live with Validity Transactions that let traders submit time-bound transactions that stay dormant until set conditions are met, such as a swap that only activates if a pool price crosses a threshold before a given block. The upgrade also adds Composite Policies to its B20 token standard, letting issuers combine KYC allowlists and sanctions blocklists with OR/AND logic without duplicating member lists, Schedule Multiplier Updates for things like stock splits, and a "seizeWithMemo" function that lets authorized administrators reassign frozen balances with an onchain record. Base also said it plans to cut block times from 2 seconds to 200 milliseconds and make smart accounts native at the protocol level in coming months.

articles.headline: The Fastest Growing Market in Tech Isn't AI
articles.blurb: Stock perpetuals on Hyperliquid and Lighter reached $67.8B in June 2026 volume, 16x tokenized equity spot, with Cerebras pre-IPO perps trading within 1.3% of its Nasdaq open and SpaceX perps accumulating $2.2B in cumulative volume pre-listing. Stablecoins have become top-10 holders of US Treasuries, ahead of China, Norway, and Switzerland, and serve as the settlement layer for the tokenized assets above them. DTCC completed its first tokenized stock and Treasury production trades in July 2026, and Bloomberg added an RWA dashboard to the Terminal powered by Allium data. JPMorgan, HSBC, BlackRock, Goldman, Stripe, and Robinhood are all active in the space, marking the shift from institutional pilot programs to production-scale deployments.

articles.headline: Blockchains Create Net New Markets
articles.blurb: Markets have always had latent demand. What throttled supply was listing committees and geographic fragmentation, not any shortage of counterparties willing to trade. Blockchains remove both constraints via permissionless issuance and global distribution, and perps, AMMs, prediction markets, and peer-to-pool lending each serve as empirical proof of this thesis. Hyperliquid's HIP-3/HIP-4 framework shows the mechanism at scale: onchain RWA perps reached a $1.4T run-rate in July 2026, and during February's oil shock, WTI found canonical price discovery on trade.xyz while CME was closed. The addressable universe extends to any oracled, two-sided exposure, including compute futures, macro indicator perps, and social trends, and the protocols that issue those markets, along with the venues that exchange them, capture the value.

articles.headline: Should Aave expand beyond Ethereum?

In looking at Aave's work with Chainlink and infrastructure like Fulcrum, which could let collateral stay on Ethereum while being used to borrow on other chains such as Arc, one could see Aave's multi-chain expansion as a business decision to go where users and liquidity already are rather than a loyalty question.

articles.headline: Agents and Programmable Cryptography
articles.blurb: AI agents operating across distributed networks need methods to collaborate without sharing private context, creating practical demand for three cryptographic techniques that have remained largely in research settings: MPC distributes private inputs across participants so no single party reconstructs others' data, FHE lets cloud services compute on encrypted data without decrypting it, and TEEs use protected hardware to isolate data from cloud operators. Concrete applications include calendar coordination that confirms mutual availability without exposing full schedules, salary comparisons that verify whether two figures fall within a $10,000 threshold without revealing exact numbers, and developer support that matches error signatures across codebases without exposing proprietary code. Agents running these computations at scale require payment infrastructure, with fast stablecoin networks and state channels as settlement rails for high-volume microtransactions between agents.

Cisco's login module checked the raw request URI while WildFly matched the decoded path, so the encoded request skipped the password check and fell into a session-continuation branch that trusted hardcoded internal usernames like viptela-reserved-cloudops. articles.headline: Solving the Identity Crisis for AI Agents

That ID is then presented to a custom STS, which verifies in its agent registry that the requested agent is allowed to run on that workflow and returns a JWT with the relevant details to the workload. To simplify adoption, Uber built a standardized Agent-to-Agent client that provides an automatic, secure-by-default path.

articles.headline: What We Should Do Instead of Trusted Cyber Access Programs and Open Weight Restrictions

Frontier labs should implement low-friction, cross-lab Know Your Customer (KYC) programs, do more to detect and block attackers, and publish time-to-detection-and-response metrics.
